newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share index climbs in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share index climbs in active trade.

text.p: Nigeria's share index rose on active Friday trading, but traders said profit-taking had begun on some of the best performers and could lead them lower in the next week.
The all-share index closed at 6,570.28 from 6,559.90 on Thursday.
Traders said small investors in search of ready funds to pay for school fees were looking at selling out of those companies that have made big gains through the year.
Cadbury, Flour Mills and Union Bank which all have large volumes of shares on the market from recent bonus issues all fell on Friday.
"The pre-Christmas search for funds may also have started early," one trader said.
Cadbury fell 20 kobo to 26.70 naira. Flour Mills was 20 kobo down at 10.80. Union Bank was down 10 kobo at 7.90 naira.
On the positive side Nestle Foods jumped 70 kobo to 33.40 naira. National Oil gained 50 kobo to 34.00 naira.
Cement shares finished strongly after recent construction contracts awarded by the Petroleum Trust Fund.
Ashaka Cement gained 35 kobo to 19.00 naira. West African Portland Cement rose 25 kobo to 34.25 naira. Benue Cement rose 20 kobo to touched 7.00 naira.
Guinness continued to drop, down 10 kobo to 8.24 naira. CFAO shed 15 kobo to 4.10 naira and Dunlop lost 10 kobo to 11.50 naira.
Despite a slightly higher nine-month after-tax profit to end-June, Vitafoam dropped 20 kobo to 4.60 naira. First Aluminium too was 20 kobo down at 4.60 naira.
